newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo shipper expects $37 mln income in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo shipper expects $37 mln income in 1997 - paper.

text.p: The Yugoslav shipper Jugooceanija of Kotor, Montenegro, reported a profit of $3 million in the first four months of the year, the Belgrade newspaper Politika reported on Tuesday.
"Jugooceanija's income in the first four months of the year was $8.2 million, with a clean profit of $3 million," Director Milivoje Jaukovic was quoted by Politika as saying.
The shipper expects total 1997 income to reach around $37 million after the deblocking of 15 of its ships with a 502,000 tonnes capacity.

Jugooceanija's ships were "frozen" by five years of war-related international sanctions against Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, which were suspended in November 1995 and lifted in October 1996.
Jugooceanija's vessels Lovcen, Durmitor, Moslavina and Zeta, which remained blocked in U.S. ports over unsettled fees, were released a few days ago, the paper said.
Lovcen, Durmitor and Moslavina are on their way to a Spanish shipyard for overhaul while Zeta will dock in the Adriatic shipyard Bijela in Boka Kotorska.
The ships were able to sail after Jugooceanija secured $950,000 to repay foreign debts as well as $600,000 for fuel, spare parts and documents, the report said.
Last year Berlinerbank of London approved a $17 million credit for Jugooceanija, which was subsequently frozen.
But a few days ago the bank informed the Kotor shipper it could use the funds to purchase ships.
"We plan to buy two new and two second hand ships, not more than ten years old," Jugooceanija's commercial director Pavle Rajman was quoted as saying.

According to the report, the company has completed the first stage of ownership transformation giving 47.7 percent of the shares to its present and former employees and 52.3 percent to the Montenegrin state and its development, pension and employment funds.
Jugooceanija's capital has been evaluated at $100 million. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
